rationale: The flagged operations expand/resolve a local path and test existence/file type. They do not read media contents or scale their byte work with media size.
ChunkedUploader.upload offloads whole-file hashing with run_in_executor; _upload_one_part offloads chunk reading the same way. The potentially large media I/O is already outside the event loop.

The standard synchronous send_message tool dispatches _send_to_platform through model_tools._run_async; these direct REST helper probes are separate from the QQ websocket adapter sender. _run_async uses the tool/worker loop and creates a fresh worker when called under an existing running loop.
The uploader flow tests cover a real temporary 8 MB file split across two parts with fake HTTP, plus group endpoint behavior. Direct-send routing/fallback tests also pass.
verification_limits: Direct-send media tests substitute the upload helper at their transport seam; actual file hashing/part reads are covered separately by ChunkedUploader tests. No slow-mount latency guarantee was measured.
candidates.unhealthy_filesystem_caveat: Path resolution, existence/type checks, and the uploader preflight stat can block on unhealthy or network-mounted filesystems despite not reading file contents. Any acceptance must be limited to this existing metadata-preflight scope.

rationale: The flagged operation is one os.path.exists metadata probe per nonempty media item. It performs no bulk file read. URL media is subsequently recognized and passed to the URL-upload path.
A missing local file produces an omission warning and continues delivery; when all media fail, the caption/message is delivered as text. Existing tests explicitly verify those preservation contracts.
The downstream local upload path already offloads content hashing and chunk reads. Profile-scoped direct-send credential tests pass alongside media delivery tests.
As with _qqbot_upload_local_file, the production direct-send entry is routed through model_tools._run_async rather than being the QQ websocket adapter sender.
verification_limits: The number of metadata probes scales with the requested attachment list; there is no claimed strict wall-clock bound. Tests use fake provider transport and do not exercise live QQ service or pathological storage.
candidates.unhealthy_filesystem_caveat: A single exists probe can still stall on unhealthy or network-backed storage. This is bounded metadata work per attachment, not a proof of nonblocking operation and not a general async-I/O allowance.
